title: Hongda Zhao
text:
About
I am a bioinformatics PhD candidate at Kyoto University and a JSPS Research Fellow (DC1), based in Kyoto, Japan.



Brief bio



My research focuses on viruses hidden in eukaryotic genomes, comparative viral genomics, and AI-assisted protein discovery. I enjoy turning large, heterogeneous biological datasets into reproducible workflows and evidence that can be inspected from more than one angle.
This site is a home for my research, publications, technical notes, and occasional observations from life beyond the computer.





Quick facts

RolePhD candidate · JSPS Research Fellow (DC1)
InterestsViral genomics · comparative genomics · protein discovery
LocationKyoto, Japan
LanguagesChinese · English · Japanese
Contactwork.hongda@gmail.com

Birds, biodiversity, and field notes

title: Hongda Zhao
text:
Research & Projects
I combine comparative genomics, phylogenetics, protein-structure analysis, and machine learning to study virus evolution and build reusable discovery systems.



Research interestsThree connected directions

Viral elements in eukaryotic genomesReconstructing past virus–host interactions from integrated viral sequences and their distribution across eukaryotic lineages.
Virus evolution and comparative genomicsUsing genome-scale and phylogenetic evidence to understand viral diversity, host range, and evolutionary history.
AI-assisted protein discoveryCombining protein language models with sequence, structure, and cluster-aware validation for interpretable discovery.




Selected projectsFrom question to evidence


Protein discovery · 2026–presentDJR-FinderAI-assisted recognition and validation of double jelly-roll proteins.

ProblemSequence divergence makes viral major capsid proteins and related double jelly-roll proteins difficult to identify reliably at scale.
My roleDesigned the end-to-end modelling and validation workflow.
ApproachFrozen ESM-2 embeddings, calibrated linear classifiers, cluster-aware data splitting, HMMER, and Foldseek.
OutcomeUnified protein recognition, capsid classification, and conditional viral taxonomy prediction in one reproducible system.

Code and manuscript links will be added when public.



Comparative genomics · 2025–presentEndogenous dsDNA viral landscapeA large-scale view of viral elements embedded in eukaryotic genomes.

ProblemEndogenous elements derived from dsDNA viruses remained poorly characterised across eukaryotes.
My roleLed dataset design, pipeline development, comparative analysis, validation, and manuscript preparation.
ApproachScreened 37,254 public eukaryotic genomes and standardised 781,111 viral regions from 7,103 assemblies.
OutcomeRevealed broad but lineage-specific accumulation and previously unrecognised virus–host associations.

PreprintPublication details



Virus–host range · 2023–2024Mirusvirus host-range researchGenomic evidence for a wider diversity and ecological range of mirusviruses.

ProblemMirusviruses were known mainly from marine metagenomes, while their potential eukaryotic hosts remained uncertain.
My roleLed the first-author computational study and integrated sequence, structure, and phylogenetic evidence.
ApproachScreened 1,901 eukaryotic genome assemblies for marker genes and examined high-confidence capsid signals and circular genomes.
OutcomeExpanded the known host range across eight eukaryotic supergroups and diverse environments.
